title: Styes and chalazia (eyelid inflammation)
intro: A stye is a painful red lump at the edge of the eyelid caused by infection of an eyelash follicle or gland. A chalazion is a firmer, usually painless lump caused by a blocked oil gland deeper in the lid. Both are common and most go away on their own with warm compresses.

sections.heading: Stye
paragraphs: A stye, or hordeolum, looks like a red, tender, swollen bump on the lid margin, sometimes with a yellow centre of pus. It results from bacterial infection, usually Staphylococcus. Eyelid inflammation called blepharitis, poor lid hygiene, touching the eyes with unwashed hands and old makeup raise the risk.

sections.heading: Chalazion
paragraphs: A chalazion develops when an oil gland in the eyelid becomes blocked and its contents leak into surrounding tissue, causing inflammation. It forms a firm round lump away from the lid edge, often painless after an initial tender period. It may press on the eye and blur vision if large. It can follow a stye.

sections.heading: Home treatment
paragraphs: Apply a clean warm compress for about ten minutes, three or four times a day, to soften the blockage and encourage drainage. Gently massage the lid afterwards. Keep the lids clean with a mild cleanser or lid wipes. Do not squeeze or pop the lump. Avoid eye makeup and contact lenses until healed.

sections.heading: Medical treatment
paragraphs: Most styes heal within one to two weeks, and chalazia may take weeks to months. If a lump persists, is very large or affects vision, a doctor can inject a steroid or make a small incision to drain it under local anaesthetic. Antibiotics are needed only for spreading infection of the eyelid or the skin around the eye.

sections.heading: When to see a doctor
paragraphs: Seek prompt care for redness and swelling that spreads over the eyelid and cheek, pain on moving the eye, fever, vision changes or a lump that bleeds or keeps coming back in the same spot, since rarely a tumour can mimic a chalazion.

examples.title: Warm compress routine
examples.text: Imagine your eyelid has a tender bump. You could use a clean warm cloth for ten minutes four times a day and wash your hands before touching the area.

examples.title: Preventing recurrence
examples.text: Suppose you get styes often. You might clean the lid margins daily, replace eye makeup regularly and ask about treatment for blepharitis.
